question: May an experimental Claw package register a stdio MCP command in the shared `mcp.servers` configuration, and what host authorization and cross-Claw sharing boundary must apply?
rationale: The branch introduces a durable core ownership model, but source inspection cannot safely choose whether arbitrary package commands are acceptable, which executable broker/allowlist should own approval, or whether global sharing is a supported product contract.

options.title: Require brokered, scoped MCP registration
options.body: Require host-authorized or allowlisted stdio registration and make shared declarations explicit before continuing this ownership slice.

options.title: Accept global experimental ownership
options.body: Deliberately allow consented Claw packages to populate the shared MCP namespace and document the resulting host-trust boundary.

options.title: Pause the MCP ownership slice
options.body: Defer this PR until the RFC or a narrower owner design establishes the command and namespace contract.

recommendation.title: Require brokered, scoped MCP registration
recommendation.body: Require host-authorized or allowlisted stdio registration and make shared declarations explicit before continuing this ownership slice.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to this PR and have already reviewed the relevant source-config and lifecycle boundaries.
